scope: Individual mathematical review of J1 and its U1/M1/P3 dependencies. No implementation, proof or existing evidence changed; no long experiments run.

findings.finding: Expanding half squared residual norm gives r^T e+e^T e/2. Differentiation gives J^T e+E^T r+E^T e. The Jacobian Gram difference is J^T E+E^T J+E^T E, while differentiating the score adds sum e_i Hessian(r_i)+sum (r_i+e_i) Hessian(e_i). Identical prior cancels in cost/score/Hessian differences, but the named GN precision requires its declared consistently represented prior precision.

Substituting e=sum e_a and E=sum E_a retains every ordered pair in E^T e and E^T E. Neither disjoint response families nor a component norm reduction removes these cross terms; beneficial cancellation can be lost. No independent-parameter premise is introduced.

For affine residuals and quadratic prior the approximate gradient is affine with matrix Phat. Stationarity at the reference optimum leaves Delta g as its intercept. Factoring Phat=P^(1/2)(I+A)P^(1/2) yields z=-(I+A)^(-1)b. Symmetric A with spectral norm at most epsilon<1 has inverse norm at most 1/(1-epsilon). The statement remains limited to interior unconstrained quadratic optima and positive definite P,Phat.

For F(theta,alpha)=gradient[pi+half||r+alpha e||^2], D_theta F at (theta*,0) is the exact Hessian H; D_alpha F is J^T e+E^T r. C1 F and nonsingular H give the stated IFT derivative. The packet correctly refrains from identifying this with GN, a finite-alpha displacement or a global minimum.

Inverting the same positive definite precision factorization and multiplying by Ghat yields (T+D)(I+A)^(-1)(T+D)^T, including transport derivative error. Taylor expansion of qhat about theta* gives the stated same-anchor defect plus Ghat times displacement and remainder. A covariance comparison cannot bound the query mean defect.

For theta=f(u) and nonsingular S=Df at the same physical anchor, covectors transform by S^T and the declared GN bilinear form by congruence S^T P S. Inverse congruence proves invariant score quadratic form and query covariance; det(S^T(Phat-lambda P)S)=det(S)^2 det(Phat-lambda P) proves generalized spectral invariance. This uses the consistently represented prior metric, not the ordinary Hessian of a newly Gaussianized nonlinear prior.

verification.method: Independent symbolic expansion, stationarity solve, matrix factorization, implicit-function hypotheses and inverse-congruence review.
verification.why_no_numeric_suite: All reviewed claims are elementary conditional identities or inequalities; numerical samples would not prove their universal statements. No implementation changed.

remaining_obligations: Positive definite reference/approximate precisions are required wherever inverse roots/covariances are used; singular weak directions are not repaired by this theorem.
Physical query and response approximations must be assessed jointly over their declared support with full transport and nuisance coupling.
Finite nonlinear fit shifts require an additional justified continuation/remainder argument or remain empirical diagnostics.
No coverage, global nonlinear optimization, lifetime evidence preservation, fixed-memory feasibility or target resource certificate follows.
